scope: Conditional simulation sensitivities prioritise evidence; they do not fit real equipment or establish realistic probability distributions.

items.title: Recovery is an operating test, not just a completed repair
items.reason: The original case restored physical capacity long before the controller confirmed it. A successful procedure and verified production capability require different evidence.
items.collect: Time-aligned commanded and delivered electrical power, independently metered hydrogen inventory/flow, isolation state, calibration/reference checks, intervention start/end, and observed post-service tests. Retain failed and censored tests.
items.boundary: Independent numerical agreement is not validation of this sensor chain. Inactive operation remains insufficient evidence.

items.title: Compatible remedies and their failure modes
items.reason: Changing remedy effectiveness can change whether continued autonomous scheduling is useful. A scalar probability cannot establish hardware compatibility.
items.collect: A cause-specific fault/remedy matrix from the equipment provider; operating and isolation prerequisites; actual attempts with outcomes, replacement identities, post-repair observations and unresolved cases.
items.boundary: Zero-success and certain-success runs bracket declared scenarios. They are not a confidence interval or a measured reliability range.

items.title: Crew access, spares and response time
items.reason: The original fixture assumes immediate crew response, a short journey and readily available module kits. Those assumptions strongly condition the value of recovery planning.
items.collect: For one candidate site per region: provider quotations, service hours and callout rules; travel and mobilisation logs; spare availability, lead times, delivery costs and access restrictions. Separate dispatch delay, travel, work and verification.
items.boundary: Regional anchor coordinates are not accessible deployment parcels. No vendor service-level commitment has been supplied.

items.title: CO₂ logistics set a production ceiling
items.reason: The 72-hour fixture supplies at most 1,100 kg CO₂, enough for 400 kg methane; the seven-day fixture supplies 2,300 kg, enough for about 836.4 kg methane. Several cases reach these ceilings, hiding the value of additional power or faster recovery.
items.collect: A site-specific delivered CO₂ specification, usable batch size, cadence, supply interruptions, minimum order and logistics cost; distinguish contracted delivery capability from the current chosen scenario. Compare changed supply scenarios with the original plant and controller policies held fixed.
items.boundary: The fixture is externally supplied CO₂, not direct-air capture. This is an inventory/material constraint, not a measured vendor supply limit.

items.title: Reactor heat retention and starting requirements
items.reason: Thermal inertia changes the value of looking ahead and the timing of energy reserves. The doubled thermal-capacity sensitivity is explicitly exploratory.
items.collect: Instrumented warm-up and cool-down sequences across ambient temperatures and operating modes, with heater/cooling input, reactor temperature and methane rate. Fit on one sequence and evaluate on independent sequences.
items.boundary: The existing 0.3 kWh/K reference and its sensitivity values are unmeasured assumptions, not a calibrated reactor range.

items.title: Forecast error and actual array output
items.reason: An irradiance forecast does not directly establish usable DC or recovery-test power. The programme keeps archive issues, publication times and forecast stress separate.
items.collect: Independent irradiance, ambient/module temperature and DC power with clipping/curtailment flags; local issue-time forecasts and observations across seasons. Preserve gap/quality flags and calibration periods before choosing held-out windows.
items.boundary: ERA5 is reanalysis. One previously used year and an assumed +50% forecast challenge do not identify error-tail probabilities or interannual uncertainty.

items.title: Economic value and site feasibility
items.reason: Changing prices can change the preferred operating objective even with an unchanged physical trace. Short conditional repair cases cannot identify annual ownership value.
items.collect: Dated asset and service quotations, land/access evidence, permitted water/CO2 supply terms, and an explicit acceptance/offtake scenario. Preserve whether each cost is fixed, usage-related or paid per event.
items.boundary: Gross methane is not certified delivered product. No income, lifetime fault rate or site rights are inferred from public map layers.

control.title: Objectives and planning approximations
control.mechanism: Greedy, methane MPC and economic MPC operate on declared horizons and information. Service policies use finite candidate sets and subjective recovery/inspection beliefs. Recovery policy version 3 records a separate post-mission verification window, retains original deadlines, and escalates unresolved testing; receipt completion never confirms capacity. Opt-in autonomy version 2 separates finite persistent equipment factors from independent bounded job multipliers, learns only from observed clocks, and preserves per-job phase correlation. Finite-model selection uses a predeclared observation-time holdout; synthetic observation fitting is not field calibration. Conditional retrieval charging can follow a qualified nominated whole-mission return for an already observed stranding; no repair or drive-readiness credit is granted.
control.boundary: Weights, priors, probe size, retries and risk budgets are policy choices. Optimality is bounded by information, terminal inventory treatment, candidate coverage and solver termination; model mismatch is separate.
control.next_data: Choose service/production objectives and acceptable uncertainty; evaluate with frozen matched information, terminal inventories and held-out stress cases. Do not infer event probabilities from illustrative belief priors.

economics.title: Prices, allocations and decision economics
economics.mechanism: Allocated ownership and max(calendar, usage) replacement allowances are separate from action-dependent inputs and wear. Repricing cannot change recorded actions.
economics.boundary: EUR defaults have no quotations, price year, location-specific tariffs or matched equipment scope. Purchased water is 12 L/kg H₂ versus 9 kg/kg reaction consumption; the additional treatment/handling allowance is not an independently tracked water process. Linear capacity scaling and wear proxies are scenario assumptions. No annual ROI can be inferred from short injected-fault windows.
economics.next_data: Matched installed quotes, utility/water/CO₂ contracts, service invoices and replacement records; explicit VAT, currency date, utilisation and equipment boundaries.

faults.title: Fault lifecycle and incidence
faults.mechanism: Scheduled disturbances have declared causes; persistent faults remain until a compatible accepted intervention. Transient timing is explicit.
faults.boundary: Fault schedules and categorical causes are test scenarios, not estimated incidence, MTBF or a complete failure-mode analysis. A contact cannot uniquely diagnose all equipment faults.
faults.next_data: Cause-coded fleet/site logs with exposure hours, censored healthy intervals, downtime and repair outcomes. Preserve common-cause failures and seasonal effects.

maintenance.title: Reliability and routine maintenance
maintenance.mechanism: Routine work, replaceable stock and duty-related wear can be accounted for; hardware failures have explicit recovery paths.
maintenance.boundary: Fixed intervals, success probabilities and calendar lives are assumptions. Preventive maintenance is not a measured hazard reduction or a physical degradation model.
maintenance.next_data: Exposure-based failure histories and maintenance manuals for the selected equipment; separate scheduled maintenance, breakdown repair and capacity ageing.

sensing.title: Measurement uncertainty and diagnosis
sensing.mechanism: Power and flow get seeded multiplicative noise. Tank noise scales with current production; battery, CO₂, temperature and hydrogen withdrawal are exact. Diagnosis compares tracking and mass-balance residuals.
sensing.boundary: Tank noise becomes zero at zero production. Differencing inventory measurements needs an uncertainty/covariance budget; two samples and a 10%/3σ threshold do not establish a field false-alarm rate.
sensing.next_data: Identify meters and independent reference channels; collect zero/span, drift, bias, covariance and time-synchronisation data over low and high flows. Validate diagnosis with blind held-out faults.

solar.title: PV conversion and clipping
solar.mechanism: Hourly tilted irradiance drives a simple NOCT temperature relation and linear power coefficient. Reference PV caps at nameplate. Detailed sections use fixed 30% diffuse contribution, uniform shade and a separate converter.
solar.boundary: Nameplate is a reference rating, not by itself a physical output ceiling. Sections have no string mismatch, diode, wind or snow model. Generic losses, section soiling and service soiling need non-overlapping definitions.
solar.next_data: Select module, mounting, converter and loss ledger together. Obtain measured POA irradiance, cell/ambient temperature, wind and unclipped DC power; validate on different seasons.

support.title: Support system and access
support.mechanism: Finite work time, shifts, inventory, transport, charging and returns can constrain service. Optional models declare which resources exist. Opt-in autonomy version 2 separates finite persistent equipment factors from independent bounded job multipliers, learns only from observed clocks, and preserves per-job phase correlation. Finite-model selection uses a predeclared observation-time holdout; synthetic observation fitting is not field calibration. Conditional retrieval charging can follow a qualified nominated whole-mission return for an already observed stranding; no repair or drive-readiness credit is granted. Optical coverage uses the actual job perform duration; completed-area brush consumption is checked directly against the resource ledger.
support.boundary: Route traversal and interlocks are ideal abstractions; no obstacles, terrain, hazardous-area qualification or physical isolation dynamics. Durations, travel and supplier capacity are illustrative. Opt-in bounded-clock factors are persistent world assumptions. Full-support reservations, actual consumption, current-only outages and right-censored observations are distinct; no job-independent empirical duration population is claimed.
support.next_data: Site layout and access survey, regional callout terms, task time/energy observations, stores policy, staffed support and communications availability. Do not combine incompatible hardware claims.

thermal.title: Reactor heat and operating envelope
thermal.mechanism: One perfectly mixed temperature; constant inputs per hour; analytic heating, reaction heat, ambient heat loss and cooling. Production requires beginning and ending temperatures in band.
thermal.boundary: C=0.3 kWh/K and UA=0.08 kW/K are unmeasured. No spatial hot spots, catalyst kinetics, feed sensible heat, pressure, conversion efficiency, condensation or purge. The 4-hour commitment is a scheduling assumption.
thermal.next_data: Obtain reactor geometry/material masses, insulation and catalyst specifications; log heater power, ambient and multiple temperatures through controlled warm-up, soak and cool-down, then separate load-step validation.

layout.title: Capacities and initial conditions
layout.mechanism: Installed capacities and starting inventories define the test plant. They are choices, not population estimates.
layout.boundary: The fixture is not a named, coherent equipment package. Changing capacity alone does not resize vessels, converters, pumps, access or thermal mass.
layout.next_data: Choose a bill of materials and electrical/material boundaries; record working versus nominal capacity and starting-state measurements.

gas-storage.title: Gas buffers and deliveries
gas-storage.mechanism: Ideal mass inventories with capacity bounds. CO₂ delivery is accepted before withdrawal; concurrent hydrogen inflow/outflow follows the execution contract. Excess delivery is rejected explicitly.
gas-storage.boundary: No pressure, temperature, compressor consumption, usable heel, leakage, boil-off, delivery purity or unloading equipment. Supply quantities and timing are scenarios, not contracted logistics.
gas-storage.next_data: Specify storage technology and operating pressure/temperature, usable mass, compression/drying power, supplier delivery constraints and metering.

atb.title: 2024 ATB utility PV plus battery
atb.finding: Assumes 85% grid-charge and 87% coupled-PV round-trip efficiency for a utility-scale reference design.
atb.applicability: Planning assumptions at a different scale and electrical boundary, not evidence that the fixture 90% is measured. Do not transplant US cost estimates.
atb.access: Official search-index extract; direct page fetch failed (502), 2026-09-12

doe-pem.title: DOE technical targets for PEM electrolysis
doe-pem.finding: The 2022 status table distinguishes stack electricity (51 kWh/kg) from system electricity (55 kWh/kg); later columns are targets. Performance, lifetime and cost must be considered together.
doe-pem.applicability: Technology benchmark, not a matched 450 kW device. No support for the fixture startup energy, minimum load, fixed efficiency curve or European installed cost.

field-review.title: Existing field realism review and sources
field-review.finding: Fourteen families reviewed; cause-specific repair, sensor identifiability and support requirements remain open.
field-review.applicability: Retained historical review, not current-run validation. Relevant current source files were reviewed again for this edition. The 31 prior findings are retained separately.

gum.title: JCGM VIM: calibration
gum.finding: Calibration establishes a measurement relationship with uncertainties under specified conditions; it differs from adjustment and verification.
gum.applicability: Terminology and measurement practice. Simulation parameter fitting additionally needs an identifiable model and held-out validation.

nist-ch4.title: NIST Chemistry WebBook: methane
nist-ch4.finding: Molecular weight 16.0425; Chase gas formation enthalpy −74.87 kJ/mol.
nist-ch4.applicability: Supports ideal stoichiometric and standard heat comparisons, not reactor thermal capacity or kinetics.

nist-co2.title: NIST Chemistry WebBook: carbon dioxide
nist-co2.finding: Molecular weight 44.0095; Chase gas formation enthalpy −393.52 kJ/mol.
nist-co2.applicability: Standard-state gas thermochemistry; pressure, kinetics and process conversion require additional models.

nist-water.title: NIST Chemistry WebBook: water
nist-water.finding: Molecular weight 18.01528; gas formation enthalpy −241.8264 kJ/mol in Chase Shomate coefficients.
nist-water.applicability: Water vapour basis. Do not substitute liquid-water enthalpy without accounting for condensation and recovery.

pv-validation.title: Sandia PV performance modelling and validation
pv-validation.finding: Reports public quality-controlled PV/weather datasets and independent blind model comparisons.
pv-validation.applicability: Useful candidate for testing a generic PV model. These observations do not describe our unnamed European array.

rsc.title: Monning et al.: three-phase CO₂ methanation kinetics
rsc.finding: Reports ideal Sabatier heat of −165 kJ/mol and studies catalyst wetting, side reactions and deactivation in a three-phase slurry system.
rsc.applicability: Supports exothermic chemistry and the importance of heat management; does not calibrate the fixture lumped thermal mass, heat loss or production envelope.
rsc.access: Primary abstract and indexed first-page PDF extract read; direct HTML returned 403, 2026-09-12

sam-pv.title: SAM / PVWatts model documentation
sam-pv.finding: Version 8 uses NOCT reference temperatures of 45°C for open-rack and 49°C for roof-mount; listed crystalline-silicon power coefficients are −0.37 and −0.35 %/°C. Module and converter models have separate boundaries.
sam-pv.applicability: Reference model assumptions, not fitted site values. Dispatch Lab is not a PVWatts implementation; its simple NOCT and fixed diffuse fraction omit several mechanisms.

soiling.title: IEA PVPS: soiling losses
soiling.finding: Soiling is spatially heterogeneous and requires local measurement; snow is a separate concern at higher latitudes.
soiling.applicability: Global annual loss estimates cannot establish a constant European daily deposition rate or a robot cleaning efficacy.

uncertainty.title: JCGM VIM: metrological compatibility
uncertainty.finding: Uncertainty of a difference depends on both uncertainties and their covariance.
uncertainty.applicability: Independent inventory differences do not inherit a percentage-of-flow uncertainty without an explicit measurement model.

nist-h2.title: NIST Chemistry WebBook: hydrogen
nist-h2.finding: Molecular weight 2.01588; standard elemental reference enthalpy zero.
nist-h2.applicability: Reference chemistry only, not an electrolyser conversion or purity guarantee.

unbound_path_notes.service_economics: Structured service price ledger, not one scalar catalogue parameter. Actual quotation lines require their own source and validity period.

release_scope: Release 1 qualifies numerical reference autonomy. These consequential empirical gaps remain open and feed Release 2 equipment-specific modelling. No new field measurements or quotations were obtained during this software release.
